implementerProof.how: Every entry of the implement handoff's proof array was driven again here, independently, in this issue's own tester container at the branch's code head (2843635fe941, unchanged by 41b400c1, which touches .legion/ alone). Entries 1, 4 and 5 (the rendered pod): a throwaway test of my own in package sandbox rendered an issue pod and the controller's pod and printed every role container's told paths with the mount holding each — all seven directories per role under /legion/scratch/<role>, each on `mount=issue at /legion subPath=""` (pvc issue-legion-legion-legion-208; the controller's own pvc issue-legion-legion-controller), no two roles sharing one, XDG_CONFIG_HOME still the in-memory config volume, workspace-init still on /home/legion/.cache, /home/legion/.local/share and /home/legion/.local/state, workspace-fetch still TMPDIR=/tmp, and uv's two directories untouched and outside every scratch. Entry 2 (a role living in that environment): instead of calling podsafety.EnsureScratch from a program, I ran the real built `legion worker-shim --pod-safety` against a fake daemon that acks its hello, with the rendered environment of a role whose scratch did not exist — it made tmp, cache, data, go/build, go/mod and bun/install/cache (0700 plus the volume's setgid, legion:legion) and the state home's omp/profiles/legion, the child's `mktemp -d` landed in TMPDIR, the child's write to XDG_CACHE_HOME succeeded, and its exit 7 came back through the shim; the hello reached the daemon only after the directories were made. Entry 3 (bun) rested on a unit assertion over the rendered script, which is not a proof of the behaviour, so its live half was run here and agreed: see the proof entry below. The implement handoff's one unproven claim that could not be driven here is the deployment's own pod.env, which no process in this repository can read; the architect recorded on 2026-10-20 at 08:10Z that it sets DISPATCH_PUBLIC_URL alone.

implementerProof.roundTwo: The implement handoff's new entry — the tester's failure fixed — was driven again here rather than taken. The diff between the head I tested in round one and this round's code head is `packages/daemon/internal/shim/shim_test.go` alone, 16 lines, the socketPath helper, with `.legion/` text beside it (`jj diff --stat -r '41b400c1d959..bd2383dae192'`), and my own red test file is byte-identical to the commit I pushed it in (`jj diff --stat -r '0b3e8b6b4fdd..6aeb521ebff2' packages/daemon/internal/shim/socketpath_test.go` is empty). So nothing of round one's acceptance proofs could have moved, and the pod-builder suite passing again in this round's module run confirms it. Its two claims I could not run, I read: internal/daemon's and internal/stream's helpers do take their base from TMPDIR (`os.MkdirTemp("")`) rather than a test's name, and the premise under its arithmetic holds — every unix socket internal/daemon binds comes through `shortTempDir`, by way of `testConfig`'s StateDir (daemon_test.go:84) or `supervisor_test.go:157` directly; the one config built on a bare `t.TempDir()` (clonecredential_test.go:53) calls `reconfigureCloneCredential` and listens on nothing. Its identical-both-ways claim I confirmed myself, and it understates the count: eight packages fail, not six, and the same 93 tests fail under both TMPDIRs, differing only in their durations.

resolvedFailures.criterion: A role living in the environment this change renders can do its ordinary work in it — the spec's "What changes", and the pull request's own bullet "The repository's own cmd/legion test suite runs inside a role container again: its unix sockets no longer depend on TMPDIR being short". The suite a role runs is the repository's, not cmd/legion's alone.
resolvedFailures.evidence: `internal/shim` does not run under the TMPDIR this change gives a role container. In this issue's tester container, at the branch's code head, `cd packages/daemon && TMPDIR=/legion/scratch/implementer/tmp go test -count=1 -p 1 ./internal/shimwire/ ./internal/shim/ ./internal/stream/` fails with 16 `bind: invalid argument` listens, every one of them a socket this package's own helper spells under TMPDIR — for example `listen on /legion/scratch/implementer/tmp/TestAdoptWorkingCopyRunsTheSharedMetaeditAndAnswersTheDaemona_c240954141/003/s: bind: invalid argument` (shim_test.go:963), 110 bytes against Linux's 107-byte sun_path. The same command with TMPDIR=/tmp, which is what a role container had before this change (it was told no temporary directory at all), passes; `internal/shimwire` and `internal/stream` pass under both, and `cmd/legion` passes under both because this pull request already fixed it there (socketDir, worker_shim_test.go). So this is a regression this change introduces, in the same class the implementer recognised and fixed in one package: `internal/shim/shim_test.go:388`'s `socketPath` is `filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "s")`, the exact helper the pull request replaced in cmd/legion. The pull request's `Fast-follow:` line names `internal/daemon/daemon_test.go`'s `shortTempDir` and `internal/stream/helpers_test.go`'s `shortSocketPath` as the remaining copies; both of those in fact bind (stream's whole suite passes under the production TMPDIR), and the package that actually breaks is named nowhere. A defect that breaks a gate is not a fast-follow. Red test, in its own commit on this branch: `packages/daemon/internal/shim/socketpath_test.go`, `TestASocketPathBindsWhereTMPDIRIsARoleContainersScratch` — it points TMPDIR at a directory as long as a role container's and listens on the path `socketPath` builds, and fails today on any machine, CI included: `cd packages/daemon && go test -count=1 -run TestASocketPathBindsWhereTMPDIRIsARoleContainersScratch ./internal/shim/` prints `listen on /tmp/73b92639f15805283e38c12e76/TestASocketPathBindsWhereTMPDIRIsARoleContainersScratchAdoptWor2572775919/001/s (111 bytes): bind: invalid argument`. Rooting this package's socket directory at /tmp the way cmd/legion's socketDir does makes it pass.
resolvedFailures.notReproducedHere: `internal/daemon` could not be judged: its suite needs Docker (testcontainers panics `rootless Docker not found`) and a role container has none. Its `shortTempDir` builds `<TMPDIR>/lgdXXXXXXXXX/worker-stream.sock`, about 63 bytes under the rendered TMPDIR, so arithmetic says it fits; CI is where it is actually exercised, and CI runs with a short TMPDIR, so nothing here proves it either way. Round two read the premise under that arithmetic and it holds: every unix socket the package binds comes through `shortTempDir` — `testConfig`'s StateDir (daemon_test.go:84), which is where the worker stream's `unix://<StateDir>/worker-stream.sock` comes from, and `supervisor_test.go:157` — and the one config built on a bare `t.TempDir()` (clonecredential_test.go:53) calls `reconfigureCloneCredential` and listens on nothing.
resolvedFailures.fixedBy: bd2383dae192, `fix(daemon): the shim package's test socket binds under a role's TMPDIR`: socketPath makes the socket's own directory under /tmp and removes it with the test, as cmd/legion's socketDir already did; everything else a test writes stays under t.TempDir(). Verified in round two — see the proof entry `the repository's own suite runs under the TMPDIR this change renders`.

proof.criterion: bun installs by copying files out of its cache rather than hardlinking them into the workspace, now that the two share one filesystem — as narrowed by the plan's spec departure to the install Legion renders itself.
proof.surface: the install script the runtime renders for a stale-plugin relaunch, rendered from this head and then run for real in this issue's tester container with the role's own rendered BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR and state home, both on the issue's volume; plus bun itself on the one-package check the plan names
proof.command: the rendered script run as `sh -c "$(cat install32.sh)" legion-plugins /bin/echo AGENT-ARGV-EXECED` with BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR=/legion/scratch/tester/bun/install/cache (it installs @sjawhar/pi-legion@10.13.0 and @sjawhar/pi-envoy@10.11.0 into /legion/scratch/tester/state/legion-plugins/g7); then `find <gen>/node_modules -type f | xargs stat -c %h | sort | uniq -c` and `stat -c 'inode=%i links=%h'` on an installed file and its cache file; and, separately, `bun add --exact --backend=copyfile is-odd@3.0.1` against `bun add --exact is-odd@3.0.1`, both with the cache on the volume, with `stat -c %h`
proof.observed: the install ran (`2 packages installed`), the generation directory and the cache were on one filesystem (`stat -c %d` 149 for both), and all 51 installed files came back with link count 1, the installed @sjawhar/pi-legion/package.json at inode 80296 against the cache's 77533 — copies, not links — and the same held on the second, warm-cache run of the script, which is the case where bun would otherwise link. The one-package check gave exactly what the plan predicted: with --backend=copyfile links=1 and an inode of its own, without it links=2 and the same inode as the cache file (77497).
proof.negativeControl: the same rendered script with the contract at 33, which is this head's: the published pi-legion declares 32, so the script printed `legion plugins: @sjawhar/pi-legion@10.13.0 declares daemon API contract 32; this daemon requires 33`, exited 1, and never exec'd the agent argv. The hardlink control is the without-flag install above: one inode shared with the cache, which is the corruption the flag exists to stop.
